---
title: "Single-seed descent vs bulk vs pedigree"
description: "When lines are derived, how genetic variance splits between and within lines, and how fast each method gets there."
---

## The idea

The three classic methods for self-pollinated crops all take a cross from F~2~ toward homozygous lines. They differ in **when** selection among lines starts and **how fast** generations are advanced.

- **Pedigree:** single plants are selected from F~2~ onward and their progeny grown as families, so selection starts early, on single plants or small rows with low heritability, usually one field generation per year.
- **Bulk:** the population is harvested in bulk each generation with little or no artificial selection, and lines are derived after several generations of selfing.
- **Single-seed descent (SSD):** one seed per plant is advanced each generation, often in a greenhouse or off-season nursery, to reach homozygosity quickly with every F~2~ plant represented. Lines are then derived and tested.

Selfing redistributes additive genetic variance. For lines derived from single F~*t*~ plants and grown to homozygosity, with σ²~A~ defined in the F~2~ and inbreeding *F* = 1 − (½)^*t*−2^ of the F~*t*~ plant relative to the F~2~,

$$
\sigma^2_{\text{among lines}} = (1 + F)\,\sigma^2_A, \qquad \sigma^2_{\text{within lines}} = (1 - F)\,\sigma^2_A .
$$

F~2~-derived lines carry only half of the eventual additive variance among them. Lines derived later carry nearly all of it (2σ²~A~). This is the genetic argument for delaying line derivation, as SSD does, and for doing it quickly.

*Source: Fehr, methods for self-pollinated species; Falconer & Mackay, chapter 15.*

## Widget

```{ojs}
import {pal, intensity} from "../js/common.js"

viewof deriv = Inputs.range([2, 8], {value: 5, step: 1, label: "Generation lines are derived from (F_t)"})
viewof vA = Inputs.range([1, 20], {value: 4, step: 0.5, label: "σ²A in the F₂"})
viewof vErr = Inputs.range([0, 40], {value: 8, step: 0.5, label: "Error variance of a line mean"})
viewof psel = Inputs.range([0.02, 0.5], {value: 0.1, step: 0.01, label: "Proportion of lines selected"})
viewof fieldGPY = Inputs.range([1, 2], {value: 1, step: 1, label: "Field generations per year (pedigree, bulk)"})
viewof ssdGPY = Inputs.range([1, 5], {value: 3, step: 1, label: "SSD generations per year"})
```

```{ojs}
partition = d3.range(2, 9).flatMap(t => {
  const F = 1 - 0.5 ** (t - 2);
  return [
    {t: `F${t}`, comp: "Among lines", value: (1 + F) * vA},
    {t: `F${t}`, comp: "Within lines", value: (1 - F) * vA}
  ];
})
Fd = 1 - 0.5 ** (deriv - 2)
among = (1 + Fd) * vA
gain = intensity(psel) * among / Math.sqrt(among + vErr)
gainF2 = intensity(psel) * vA / Math.sqrt(vA + vErr)
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  height: 300,
  marginLeft: 50,
  x: {label: "Generation lines are derived from", domain: d3.range(2, 9).map(t => `F${t}`)},
  y: {label: "Additive variance at homozygosity", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Among lines", "Within lines"], range: [pal[0], pal[3]]},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(partition, {x: "t", y: "value", fill: "comp", insetLeft: 2, insetRight: 2, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.t}-derived lines\n${d.comp}: ${d.value.toFixed(2)}`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0]),
    Plot.ruleX([`F${deriv}`], {stroke: "currentColor", strokeOpacity: 0.15, strokeWidth: 40})
  ]
})
```

```{ojs}
md`F${deriv}-derived lines: variance among lines = **${among.toFixed(2)}** (${(100 * among / (2 * vA)).toFixed(0)}% of the total 2σ²<sub>A</sub>). Expected gain from selecting the best ${(psel * 100).toFixed(0)}% of lines: **${gain.toFixed(2)}**, compared with **${gainF2.toFixed(2)}** for F2-derived lines.`
```

### Time to derive lines

```{ojs}
timing = [
  {method: "Pedigree", years: (deriv - 2) / fieldGPY, note: "selection on plants and families every generation"},
  {method: "Bulk", years: (deriv - 2) / fieldGPY, note: "little selection until lines are derived"},
  {method: "Single-seed descent", years: (deriv - 2) / ssdGPY, note: "every F₂ plant represented"}
]

Plot.plot({
  height: 170,
  marginLeft: 140,
  x: {label: `Years from F₂ to F${deriv} plants`, grid: true},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(timing, {x: "years", y: "method", fill: pal[0], insetTop: 4, insetBottom: 4, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.method}: ${d.years.toFixed(1)} years\n${d.note}`}),
    Plot.text(timing, {x: "years", y: "method", text: d => `${d.years.toFixed(1)} yr`, dx: 6, textAnchor: "start"}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

## Things to try

- Move derivation from F~2~ to F~6~. Variance among lines climbs from σ²~A~ toward 2σ²~A~, and so does the expected gain from selecting among them.
- Raise the error variance. Gains fall at every derivation generation, but the relative advantage of late derivation widens, from about 1.4× with no error toward 2× when error dominates.
- Set SSD to 1 generation per year. SSD loses its speed advantage, leaving only its genetic advantage of keeping every F~2~ plant represented.
